# no-inline-html

- ID: `MD033`
- Category: HTML
- Default: on, severity warning
- Fixable: no
- Tags: `html`

Documents contain no raw HTML elements other than allowed ones.

## Why

Raw HTML is not plain Markdown, and it does not carry over to output formats
other than HTML.

## Options

Set them under `rules.no-inline-html.options`.

- `allowed_elements` (`string[]`, default `[]`): HTML elements to allow, in any
  case.
- `table_allowed_elements` (`string[]`, defaults to the value of
  `allowed_elements`): HTML elements to allow in tables, in any case.

## Fix

There is no automatic fix.

## Example

This document breaks the rule:

```markdown
# Guide

Press <kbd>Enter</kbd> to continue.
```

gomdlint reports:

```text
3:7 HTML element 'kbd' is not allowed
```

This document follows the rule:

```markdown
# Guide

Press **Enter** to continue.
```

## Configure

```yaml
rules:
  no-inline-html:
    options:
      allowed_elements: []
```

Under `rules`, `no-inline-html: false` turns the rule off and
`no-inline-html: error` reports its findings as errors. The flag
`--disable no-inline-html` turns it off for one run.

## Silence one line

```markdown
<!-- markdownlint-disable-next-line no-inline-html -->
```
